current.description: Signal is the gold standard for private communication on the internet. Built and operated by the nonprofit Signal Technology Foundation, Signal offers end-to-end encrypted messaging and calling with no ads, no trackers, and no data collection. The app is free, the protocol is open source, and the organization is funded by donations — which is what keeps it independent and accountable to users instead of advertisers or acquirers.

benefits.name: The Weekly Thing, read or heard
benefits.line: Every issue arrives by email and on the website, and each one has an audio edition you can play in any podcast app.

benefits.name: Thingy
benefits.line: Jamie's agent sidekick, who knows every issue of the Weekly Thing, every blog post, and every episode of Another Thing. Ask him anything about the archive.

benefits.name: Release Notes
benefits.line: A journal that comes to you. Each morning an email arrives with today’s number as the subject, and your reply is the entry: a line or a page, photos, a voice memo. Any stretch of days can become a book to read or print.

benefits.name: Thingy, upgraded
benefits.line: Supporting Members get Claude Opus, the strongest model, answering their questions, and double the daily allowance for conversations and archive tools.

benefits.name: Commentary in your Release Notes books
benefits.line: When you make a book in Release Notes, Claude can read the notes and add commentary and annotation alongside them, for up to ten books a year.

benefits.name: A giving badge in Release Notes
benefits.line: Release Notes marks each year you give with a badge naming that year’s nonprofit, and your birthday email thanks you for it.
